plan.text: Main route: North plays D3; South takes DQ with DA, so South leads next. Try to develop four club tricks: South cashes CA and CK, then leads C4 toward dummy’s CQ. If CQ wins, dummy leads C2 toward South’s C8. This uses CA, CK, C4, CQ, C2 and C8 across the two hands; the fourth club trick depends on the defenders’ club holdings, which are unknown. If that route works, the four clubs plus DK, HA, HK and SA make nine tricks. After the club sequence, South can cash DK, lead HA for dummy’s HK, then dummy leads a spade toward SA. Reassess if the clubs do not cooperate; do not treat the proposed line as observed play.

advice.publicReason: Play the lowest diamond, D3, preserving dummy’s D8, D6 and D5. South can take West’s DQ with DA and retain DK as a later winner.
